newsitem.title: USA: IMF's Camdessus welcomes Thai economic package.
newsitem.headline: IMF's Camdessus welcomes Thai economic package.

text.p: International Monetary Fund (IMF) Managing Director Michel Camdessus said on Tuesday he welcomed the Thai government's tough package of economic reforms and was confident it would find international support.

"I greatly welcome today's important announcement by Thai authorities aimed at overcoming present economic problems in Thailand through the introduction of a comprehensive package of policies," Camdessus said in a statement.

The Thai government earlier on Tuesday unveiled a harsh set of reforms to revitalise its ailing economy. It includes the suspension of operations of more than half the nation's finance companies, a three percentage point increase in value-added tax and strict monetary and fiscal targets for the next few years.

Camdessus commended the package, aimed at ensuring some $15 billion in loans the government hopes to get from the IMF and foreign nations, for its focus on "immediate and sweeping measures" to keep Thailand's financial system afloat.

"I found particularly appropriate the adoption of a comprehensive restructuring of troubled financial institutions, as this is essential to lay the basis for the re-establishment of a sound financial sector," he said.
Camdessus said he expected that the package, which still has to be endorsed by the IMF Executive Board, would "decisively contribute to stability in financial markets in Asia".
